```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here)
  library(data.table)
})
here::i_am("reports-src/slides.qmd")
source(here("R/utils/config.R"))
load_config()
invisible(list2env(
  readRDS(get_data_path("outputs", "summary_env")), environment()
))

# Formatting only: every number comes from summary_env.rds (08)
num.fn <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))
}
ci.fn <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sprintf("[%s, %s]", num.fn(x$lower, digits), num.fn(x$upper, digits))
}
p.fn <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) return("p\u00a0<\u00a0.001")
  # Non-breaking spaces keep "p = .017" on one line
  sub("0.", ".", sprintf(if (p < 0.1) "p\u00a0=\u00a0%.3f" else
    "p\u00a0=\u00a0%.2f", p), fixed = TRUE)
}
loss.fn <- function(x) num.fn(-x$estimate)
loss_ci.fn <- function(x) {
  sprintf("[%s, %s]", num.fn(-x$upper), num.fn(-x$lower))
}
pct.fn <- function(count, n) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * count / n)
# Bold marks a test whose 95% CI excludes no effect (0, or 1 for a ratio)
bold.fn <- function(text, x, null = 0) {
  if (x$lower > null || x$upper < null) sprintf("**%s**", text) else text
}
# A test result: estimate, 95% CI and, when asked, p; bold as above
res.fn <- function(x, null = 0, with_p = FALSE) {
  text <- paste(num.fn(x$estimate), ci.fn(x))
  if (with_p) text <- paste0(text, ", ", p.fn(x$p))
  bold.fn(text, x, null)
}
# Raw memory results are per upsit_step points higher; the slides read them
# per points lower, as 08 does for per_lower
flip.fn <- function(x) {
  list(estimate = -x$estimate, lower = -x$upper, upper = -x$lower, p = x$p)
}
# The same for a change reported as a loss (sign flipped)
loss_res.fn <- function(x, with_p = FALSE) {
  text <- paste(loss.fn(x), loss_ci.fn(x))
  if (with_p) text <- paste0(text, ", ", p.fn(x$p))
  bold.fn(text, x)
}
big.fn <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")

traj <- config$trajectories
age.lst <- trajectories$age
total.dt <- age.lst$total
classes.dt <- age.lst$classes
main.dt <- classes.dt[which.max(n)]
compared <- class_pathology$age$compared
faster.dt <- classes.dt[group == compared]
other.dt <- classes.dt[!group %in% c(main.dt$group, compared)]
at.fn <- function(g) pathology$at_slopes[group == g]
class_path.dt <- class_pathology$age$summary
years.lst <- trajectories$years_since_baseline
same_class_n <- class_agreement[
  class_age == class_years_since_baseline, sum(N)
]
selected.v <- unlist(traj$selected_model)

cog <- cognition
step <- cog$upsit_step
low <- cog$per_lower
delayed <- "delayed_memory_index_score_60_69"
immediate <- "immediate_memory_index_score_60_69"
total <- "total_scale_index_score_60_69"
coupling.dt <- cog$coupling$slopes
r.fn <- function(score_col) coupling.dt[coupling.dt$score == score_col]
horizon <- cog$mci_horizon
risk.fn <- function(lvl) horizon$incidence[level == lvl]

cx <- classes_extra
prof.fn <- function(lbl, g) cx$profile[panel == lbl & group == g]
amyloid_faster <- prof.fn("Amyloid positive", compared)
amyloid_main <- prof.fn("Amyloid positive", main.dt$group)
apoe_faster <- prof.fn("APOE ε4 carrier", compared)
apoe_main <- prof.fn("APOE ε4 carrier", main.dt$group)
tau.dt <- cx$at_groups[grepl("T\\+$", level)]
tau_main <- tau.dt[startsWith(as.character(group), main.dt$group), sum(N)]
first_faster.dt <- cx$diagnoses[
  startsWith(as.character(panel), compared) & group == "First"
]
reduced_faster <- first_faster.dt[level != "Normosmia", sum(N)]
mem.fn <- function(g) cx$memory[class == g]
mem_diff.fn <- function(g) {
  m <- mem.fn(g)
  loss_res.fn(list(estimate = m$slope_diff, lower = m$slope_diff_lower,
                   upper = m$slope_diff_upper, p = m$slope_diff_p),
              with_p = TRUE)
}
mem_loss.fn <- function(g) {
  m <- mem.fn(g)
  sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", num.fn(-m$slope), num.fn(-m$slope_upper),
          num.fn(-m$slope_lower))
}
per_year.dt <- cx$sample[panel == "UPSIT tests per year"]
pause.v <- as.integer(as.character(per_year.dt[N == 0, x]))

md <- modifiers
mod.fn <- function(t) md$modifiers[term == t]
prog.fn <- function(g) md$progression[group == g]
adiff.fn <- function(s) md$amyloid_diff[status == s]

# Claims the slides make, checked against the numbers
stopifnot(
  length(pause.v) > 0, all(diff(pause.v) == 1),
  mem.fn(compared)$slope_diff_lower < 0, mem.fn(compared)$slope_diff_upper > 0,
  mem.fn(other.dt$group)$slope_diff_upper < 0,
  mod.fn("apoe_carrier")$lower < 0, mod.fn("apoe_carrier")$upper > 0,
  mod.fn("female")$lower < 0, mod.fn("female")$upper > 0,
  prog.fn("A+ MCI")$estimate == min(md$progression$estimate),
  adiff.fn("MCI")$upper < 0,
  all(grepl("_slope_", selected.v)),
  pathology$amyloid$difference$upper < 0, pathology$tau$difference$upper < 0,
  low$h1[[delayed]]$lower < 0, low$h1[[delayed]]$upper > 0,
  low$h2[[delayed]]$upper > 0, low$h2[[delayed]]$p > 0.05,
  all(coupling.dt$lower > 0),
  low$h3$main$lower > 1, low$h3$amyloid$lower > 1,
  cog$amyloid_hr$lower > 1,
  nrow(risk.fn("low")) == 1, nrow(risk.fn("high")) == 1
)
```

# Does everyone's sense of smell change the same way? {.divider data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Smell trajectories"}

Groups of people with similar smell trajectories,\
and who is in each group

## Latent class mixed model {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Method"}

- Finds subgroups of people whose UPSIT changes with age in a similar way
- Each subgroup has its own average curve;\
  each person is assigned to their most likely subgroup
- People can vary around their subgroup's curve (random intercept and slope)
- We compared 1 to 5 subgroups and kept `r age.lst$n_classes`:\
  the best fit, with clearly separated subgroups
- `r age.lst$participants` people with 2 or more UPSIT tests

::: {.notes}
lcmm::hlme, maximum likelihood, `r age.lst$n_starts` random starts per model.
Grid: 1 to 5 classes × linear or quadratic × no random effects, intercept,
or intercept and slope. Selected: `r tolower(age.lst$degree)`, random
intercept and slope (one covariance across classes), by BIC, mean posterior
probability (`r num.fn(age.lst$posterior_range[1])` to
`r num.fn(age.lst$posterior_range[2])`) and class size. Age as
(age − `r traj$age_centre`) / `r traj$time_divisor`. INTREPAD 3-month retest
left out.
:::

## Most people keep high smell scores; one in `r round(age.lst$participants / faster.dt$n)` declines faster {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Smell trajectories"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people, UPSIT (0 to 40). Group means with 95%% confidence bands; faint lines: each person.<br>Faster decline: %d people. Floor: %d people, low scores from the first test.", age.lst$participants, faster.dt$n, other.dt$n)'
knitr::include_graphics(age.lst$slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Thick lines: each group's average curve with its 95% band. Faint lines: each
person, in their group's colour.

Each person is placed in the group they most probably belong to; the
average probability of that placement is `r num.fn(classes.dt[group == main.dt$group, posterior_mean])`
in the main group, `r num.fn(faster.dt$posterior_mean)` in the faster-decline
group and `r num.fn(other.dt$posterior_mean)` in the floor group.

The floor group (`r other.dt$n` people) is not declining fast: it scores near
the bottom of the scale from the first test.
:::

## The same groups over years of follow-up {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Check"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people, adjusted for age at the first test (curves for age %.0f). %s are in the same group as on age.", years.lst$participants, years.lst$total$age_mean, pct.fn(same_class_n, years.lst$participants))'
knitr::include_graphics(years.lst$slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
The same kind of model on years since the first test instead of age, with
age at the first test (and its change over time) shared by all groups:
`r years.lst$n_classes` groups, `r tolower(years.lst$degree)`.

Group sizes on this scale: `r paste(sprintf("%s %d", tolower(years.lst$classes$group), years.lst$classes$n), collapse = ", ")`.
`r pct.fn(same_class_n, years.lst$participants)` of people are in the same
group on both scales; the slides use the groups on age.
:::

## Describing the groups {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Method"}

- Share of each group that is amyloid positive, tau positive,\
  APOE ε4 carrier and female, with 95% confidence intervals
- Olfactory diagnosis from the UPSIT norms\
  at each person's first and last test
- Delayed memory over time by group: linear mixed model,\
  adjusted for age, sex, education, RBANS version and practice effects
- The faster-decline and floor groups have `r faster.dt$n` and
  `r other.dt$n` people:\
  shares are described, not tested

::: {.notes}
Shares: Wilson 95% intervals (prop.test without continuity correction).
Amyloid (Centiloid > `r pathology$amyloid_cutoff`) and tau
(meta‑ROI SUVR > `r pathology$tau_cutoff`) at the first PET, in people with
PET.
Diagnoses as recorded with each UPSIT (normosmia to anosmia).

Memory: nlme::lme, REML. RBANS delayed memory index (60–69 norms) ~ years
since the first UPSIT × group + (age at the first UPSIT + sex + education)
× years + version (A to D) + practice (first RBANS vs later); random
intercept and slope per person. Differences in yearly change against the
main group. `r cx$memory_n$participants` people,
`r big.fn(cx$memory_n$visits)` RBANS visits from the first UPSIT on.
:::

## Faster decline: `r sprintf("%.0f%%", amyloid_faster$pct)` amyloid positive, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", amyloid_main$pct)` in the main group {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Who is in each group"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Share of each group with 95%% confidence intervals; counts beside. Amyloid and tau at the first PET scan, in people with PET.<br>APOE ε4: %s of the faster-decline group, %s of the main group. The two smaller groups are too small to compare.", sprintf("%.0f%%", apoe_faster$pct), sprintf("%.0f%%", apoe_main$pct))'
knitr::include_graphics(cx$profile_slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Each dot is the share of a group with that characteristic, the line its 95%
confidence interval; the counts are beside it.

Amyloid and tau are known only for people with PET:
`r class_path.dt[group == main.dt$group, n_pet]` in the main group,
`r class_path.dt[group == compared, n_pet]` in the faster-decline group and
`r class_path.dt[group == other.dt$group, n_pet]` in the floor group.

With so few people in the two smaller groups the intervals overlap widely;
the shares are described, not compared with a test.
:::

## Memory declined faster only in the floor group, of `r other.dt$n` people {data-eyebrow="Part 1 · Memory by group"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Delayed memory index points lost a year: main %s, faster decline %s, floor %s.<br>Extra loss a year, floor against main: %s (%d people). %d people, %s RBANS visits; curves for age %g.", mem_loss.fn(main.dt$group), mem_loss.fn(compared), mem_loss.fn(other.dt$group), mem_diff.fn(other.dt$group), other.dt$n, cx$memory_n$participants, big.fn(cx$memory_n$visits), traj$age_centre)'
knitr::include_graphics(cx$memory_slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Lines: predicted delayed memory for each group, for age `r traj$age_centre`
at the first smell test, average sex and education, RBANS version A and no
practice gain, with 95% bands.

At the first smell test the groups did not clearly differ in delayed memory,
difference from the main group: faster decline
`r res.fn(with(mem.fn(compared), list(estimate = baseline_diff, lower = baseline_lower, upper = baseline_upper, p = baseline_p)), with_p = TRUE)`,
floor `r res.fn(with(mem.fn(other.dt$group), list(estimate = baseline_diff, lower = baseline_lower, upper = baseline_upper, p = baseline_p)), with_p = TRUE)`.

The floor result rests on `r other.dt$n` people and is one of several
comparisons, with no correction for multiple testing.
:::

# Is faster smell loss a sign of Alzheimer's pathology? {.divider data-eyebrow="Part 2 · Smell and pathology"}

Amyloid and tau on PET, APOE ε4, sex,\
and later progression to MCI

## Linear mixed models {data-eyebrow="Part 2 · Method"}

- UPSIT over years since the first test,\
  with a random intercept and slope per person
- Amyloid × time tests whether yearly change differs by amyloid status;\
  tau in a separate model
- Positive at the first PET: Centiloid > `r pathology$amyloid_cutoff`; tau meta‑ROI SUVR > `r pathology$tau_cutoff`
- Adjusted for age at the first test and sex
- `r pathology$participants` people with PET

::: {.notes}
lcmm::hlme (one class), maximum likelihood, Wald 95% CIs. Fixed effects:
years + marker + marker × years + age at first test + sex, each covariate
× years. Random intercept and slope, unstructured. Continuous markers:
Centiloid per `r pathology$centiloid_step`, SUVR per `r pathology$tau_step`.
A/T groups in one model, in place of the amyloid or tau term.
:::

## Smell declines faster with amyloid and with tau {data-eyebrow="Part 2 · Amyloid and tau"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people with PET. Extra UPSIT points lost a year: amyloid %s, tau %s.<br>%d tau positive; PET came a median of %.1f years after the first smell test.", pathology$participants, loss_res.fn(pathology$amyloid$difference), loss_res.fn(pathology$tau$difference), pathology$tau_positive, pathology$years_to_pet_median)'
knitr::include_graphics(pathology$slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Lines: predicted UPSIT over years since the first test by status at the
first PET scan, with 95% bands. `r big.fn(pathology$assessments)` tests from
`r pathology$participants` people.

At the first test, amyloid-positive and negative people scored about the
same, a difference in UPSIT points of
`r res.fn(pathology$amyloid$baseline, with_p = TRUE)`. The difference is in
how fast they decline.

As continuous measures, extra UPSIT points lost a year: per
`r pathology$centiloid_step` Centiloid `r loss_res.fn(pathology$amyloid$per_step)`;
per `r pathology$tau_step` tau SUVR `r loss_res.fn(pathology$tau$per_step)`.
Adding APOE ε4 and education: amyloid
`r loss_res.fn(pathology$amyloid$sensitivity)`, tau
`r loss_res.fn(pathology$tau$sensitivity)`.

PET came a median of `r num.fn(pathology$years_to_pet_median, 1)` years after
the first smell test; for `r pathology$pet_after_last_upsit` people it came
after their last one.
:::

the A/T groups in place of amyloid or tau; these are rates, not differences.

A−T+ (`r pathology$at_sizes[group == "A-T+", N]` people) is too small to
model. A+T+ rests on `r at.fn("A+T+")$participants` people, hence its wide
interval.
:::

## APOE ε4, sex and progression to MCI {data-eyebrow="Part 2 · Method"}

- UPSIT over years since the first test, linear mixed models as before
- APOE ε4 × time and sex × time test whether yearly change\
  differs by carrier status or by sex;\
  adjusted for age at the first test
- Progression: four groups by amyloid status and by a later MCI
  diagnosis,\
  each with its own starting level and yearly change;\
  adjusted for age at the first test and sex
- `r md$n$participants` people; `r md$n$progression_participants` with PET
  for progression

::: {.notes}
nlme::lme, REML, Wald 95% CIs; random intercept and slope per person,
unstructured. APOE and sex: UPSIT ~ years + (APOE ε4 + female + age at the
first test) × years, APOE and sex centred at their sample means, so the
years term is the average yearly change. Progression: UPSIT ~ 0 + group +
group × years + (age at the first test + sex) × years; groups A− or A+ at
the first PET × stayed unimpaired or diagnosed with MCI (first MCI visit in
the study's MCI review; `r md$n$reverted_left_out` reverted cases left out).
:::

## No clear difference in smell decline by APOE ε4 or by sex {data-eyebrow="Part 2 · APOE and sex"}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .red}
**Everyone**

[`r loss.fn(mod.fn("Average yearly change"))`]{.big} [UPSIT points lost a year]{.unit}

95% CI `r loss_ci.fn(mod.fn("Average yearly change"))`
:::

::: {.card .teal}
**APOE ε4 carriers**

[`r loss.fn(mod.fn("apoe_carrier"))`]{.big} [extra points a year]{.unit}

`r bold.fn(paste0("95% CI ", loss_ci.fn(mod.fn("apoe_carrier")), ", ", p.fn(mod.fn("apoe_carrier")$p)), mod.fn("apoe_carrier"))`
:::

::: {.card .teal}
**Women**

[`r loss.fn(mod.fn("female"))`]{.big} [extra points a year]{.unit}

`r bold.fn(paste0("95% CI ", loss_ci.fn(mod.fn("female")), ", ", p.fn(mod.fn("female")$p)), mod.fn("female"))`
:::
:::

[`r md$n$participants` people. Extra loss against non-carriers and against
men.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
"Everyone" is the average yearly loss across the `r md$n$participants`
people. The other two cards are the extra loss a year in carriers against
non-carriers, and in women against men, from the same model, adjusted for
age at the first test. A carrier has one or two ε4 alleles.
:::

## Smell fell fastest with both amyloid and a later MCI diagnosis {data-eyebrow="Part 2 · Progression to MCI"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people with PET. UPSIT points lost a year: amyloid positive and later MCI %s %s.<br>Extra loss with amyloid: stayed unimpaired %s; diagnosed with MCI %s.", md$n$progression_participants, loss.fn(prog.fn("A+ MCI")), loss_ci.fn(prog.fn("A+ MCI")), loss_res.fn(adiff.fn("stayed"), with_p = TRUE), loss_res.fn(adiff.fn("MCI"), with_p = TRUE))'
knitr::include_graphics(md$progression_slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Lines: predicted UPSIT for each group, for age `r traj$age_centre` at the
first test and average sex, with 95% bands. Amyloid status at the first PET
scan; MCI from the study's MCI review.

UPSIT points lost a year: A− stayed unimpaired `r loss.fn(prog.fn("A- stayed"))`
`r loss_ci.fn(prog.fn("A- stayed"))` (`r prog.fn("A- stayed")$n` people),
A+ stayed `r loss.fn(prog.fn("A+ stayed"))` `r loss_ci.fn(prog.fn("A+ stayed"))`
(`r prog.fn("A+ stayed")$n`), A− MCI `r loss.fn(prog.fn("A- MCI"))`
`r loss_ci.fn(prog.fn("A- MCI"))` (`r prog.fn("A- MCI")$n`), A+ MCI
`r loss.fn(prog.fn("A+ MCI"))` `r loss_ci.fn(prog.fn("A+ MCI"))`
(`r prog.fn("A+ MCI")$n`).

Progression is known only after the fact and the MCI groups are small, so
these slopes describe the groups; they do not predict who will progress.
:::

# Does poorer smell come with memory decline and MCI? {.divider data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Smell, memory and MCI"}

Delayed memory on the RBANS\
and diagnoses of mild cognitive impairment

## Regression and linear mixed models {data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Method"}

- At the first visit: linear regression of RBANS delayed memory on UPSIT
- Over time: RBANS scores with a random intercept and slope per person
- UPSIT × time tests whether people with lower UPSIT decline faster
- Adjusted for age, sex, education, RBANS version and practice effects
- `r cog$rbans$participants` people, `r big.fn(cog$rbans$visits)` RBANS visits

::: {.notes}
Over time: nlme::lme, REML; RBANS ~ years × UPSIT + (age + sex +
education) × years + version (A to D) + practice (first RBANS vs later);
random intercept and slope, unstructured. RBANS delayed memory index, 60–69
norms (not age-adjusted). At the first visit: linear regression with the same
covariates. Sensitivity models add APOE ε4.
:::

## Poorer smell: no memory difference at the first test and no clear faster decline {data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Smell and memory"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people. Per %d UPSIT points lower, difference at the first test: %s; extra points lost a year: %s.", cog$rbans$participants, step, res.fn(low$h1[[delayed]], with_p = TRUE), loss_res.fn(low$h2[[delayed]], with_p = TRUE))'
knitr::include_graphics(cog$memory_slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Lines: predicted delayed memory for people at the 25th and 75th percentiles
of the first UPSIT, for average age, sex and education, with 95% bands.

On average, delayed memory fell `r num.fn(-cog$memory_annual_change$estimate)`
points a year; a second RBANS scored `r num.fn(cog$memory_retest$estimate)`
points higher from practice.

Per `r step` UPSIT points lower, extra points lost a year on the other RBANS
scores: immediate memory `r loss_res.fn(low$h2[[immediate]], with_p = TRUE)`,
total scale `r loss_res.fn(low$h2[[total]], with_p = TRUE)`.
With APOE ε4 added: at the first visit `r res.fn(flip.fn(cog$h1_sensitivity), with_p = TRUE)`;
extra loss `r loss_res.fn(flip.fn(cog$h2_sensitivity), with_p = TRUE)`.

In people with PET, extra loss per `r step` points lower:
`r loss_res.fn(low$h2_pet_sample, with_p = TRUE)` without amyloid status and
`r loss_res.fn(low$h2_amyloid, with_p = TRUE)` with it. Amyloid-positive
people lost `r num.fn(-cog$memory_amyloid_slope$estimate)` more points a year
(`r p.fn(cog$memory_amyloid_slope$p)`).
:::

## Bivariate linear mixed model {data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Method"}

- UPSIT and RBANS modelled together in one linear mixed model
- Random slopes: each person's own rate of change in smell and in memory
- Result: the correlation between the two rates across people
- Adjusted for age, sex, education, RBANS version and practice effects
- `r cog$coupling$participants` people; 95% CIs by bootstrap

::: {.notes}
`r cd <- cog$coupling$delayed` How the slope correlation was calculated
(delayed memory; the other scores use the same model).

Data: one long table. UPSIT rows are the trajectory sample's tests
(`r cd$participants` people with 2+ UPSIT, INTREPAD 3-month retest left out;
`r big.fn(cd$upsit_assessments)` rows). RBANS rows are every visit of the
same people with a delayed memory score (`r big.fn(cd$rbans_visits)` rows;
`r cd$rbans_before_first_upsit` visits before the first UPSIT kept at
negative time). An indicator marks the outcome of each row. Time is years
since the person's first UPSIT, in decades for fitting.

Fixed effects, separate for each outcome: intercept, slope over time, age at
the first UPSIT ((age − `r traj$age_centre`) / `r traj$time_divisor`), sex,
education. RBANS rows only: test version (B, C, D against A) and practice
(0 at the first RBANS, 1 after).

Random effects per person: UPSIT intercept, UPSIT slope, RBANS intercept,
RBANS slope, with an unstructured 4 × 4 covariance (pdSymm). Residuals
independent, with their own variance per outcome (varIdent; RBANS residual
SD `r num.fn(cd$residual_ratio, 1)` times UPSIT's). Fitted with nlme::lme,
REML.
:::

## Within a person, smell and memory decline together {data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Smell and memory"}

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people; each point is one person’s estimated yearly change; dashed lines: no change.<br>Correlation of the two rates: delayed memory %s, immediate memory %s, total scale %s.", cog$coupling$participants, res.fn(r.fn(delayed)), res.fn(r.fn(immediate)), res.fn(r.fn(total)))'
knitr::include_graphics(cog$coupling$slide_figure)
```

::: {.notes}
Each dot is one person's estimated yearly change in smell and in delayed
memory. Dashed lines: no change; the shaded corner is where both decline.
The line is fitted through the dots. The dots are shrunk toward the average,
so they show the direction of the correlation, not its strength.

Estimate: the covariance of the two random slopes is
`r num.fn(cd$slope_cov)` per year² (UPSIT points × index points); slope SDs
`r num.fn(cd$slope_sd_upsit)` UPSIT points and
`r num.fn(cd$slope_sd_rbans)` index points a year. Covariance divided by the
two SDs gives the correlation, `r num.fn(r.fn(delayed)$estimate)`; it does
not depend on the time unit. Other correlations are small: intercepts
`r num.fn(cd$intercept_cor)`, intercepts with slopes at most
`r num.fn(cd$max_level_rate_cor)`.

95% CI `r ci.fn(r.fn(delayed))`: people resampled with replacement
`r big.fn(cog$coupling$bootstrap_reps)` times (a person drawn twice enters as
two people), the model refitted each time, 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles;
`r cd$failed` failed fits. Bootstrap because nlme's own intervals for
variance components failed for some scores.

Reading: association between person-level rates over the same period; it
says nothing about which declines first. Assumes a straight-line change per
person; the CI is wide because each person's rate rests on few visits.
:::

## Cox proportional hazards models {data-eyebrow="Part 3 · Method"}

- Time from the first UPSIT to the first MCI diagnosis
- Hazard ratio of MCI per `r step` points lower UPSIT at the first test
- Adjusted for age, sex and education;\
  then also for amyloid status, in people with PET
- People without MCI are followed to their last visit\
  or to the last MCI review (`r format(cog$mci$coverage_end, "%B %Y")`)
- `r low$h3$main$n` people, `r low$h3$main$events` with MCI

::: {.notes}
survival::coxph. Time from the first UPSIT to the first MCI visit; people
without MCI are followed to the earlier of their last RBANS and the last MCI
review. `r cog$mci$reverted` people whose MCI reverted to normal are left
out. Sensitivity model adds APOE ε4.
:::

```{r}

#| fig-cap: !expr 'sprintf("%d people, %d with MCI. Hazard ratio per %d UPSIT points lower: %s.<br>By %d years: %s with MCI at UPSIT %d, %s at UPSIT %d; %d people still followed.", low$h3$main$n, low$h3$main$events, step, res.fn(low$h3$main, null = 1, with_p = TRUE), horizon$years, sprintf("%.0f%%", risk.fn("low")$fit), risk.fn("low")$upsit, sprintf("%.0f%%", risk.fn("high")$fit), risk.fn("high")$upsit, horizon$at_risk)'
```

Curves: predicted share with MCI over time for people at the 25th and 75th
percentiles of the first UPSIT, for average age, sex and education, with 95%
bands.

By `r horizon$years` years, `r horizon$at_risk` people were still followed
and `r horizon$events` of the `r low$h3$main$events` diagnoses had happened.

Proportional hazards held for UPSIT (`r p.fn(cog$h3$main$ph_p_upsit)`), not
for education. With APOE ε4 added, hazard ratio per `r step` points lower
`r res.fn(low$h3$sensitivity, null = 1, with_p = TRUE)`.
:::

# What we found {data-eyebrow="Summary"}

- **Most people keep their sense of smell; one in `r round(age.lst$participants / faster.dt$n)` declines faster**\
  `r sprintf("%.0f%%", amyloid_faster$pct)` of the faster group amyloid positive, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", amyloid_main$pct)` of the main group
- **Smell declines faster with amyloid and tau, not with APOE ε4 or sex**\
  `r loss.fn(pathology$amyloid$difference)` and `r loss.fn(pathology$tau$difference)` extra points a year; fastest with amyloid and later MCI
- **Poorer smell, higher risk of MCI**\
  `r round(100 * (low$h3$main$estimate - 1))`% higher risk per `r step` UPSIT points lower, unchanged by amyloid status
- **Within a person, smell and memory decline together**\
  correlation `r num.fn(r.fn(delayed)$estimate)` for delayed memory; no clear link with the first UPSIT score

## What these results cannot tell us yet {data-eyebrow="Summary · Limits"}

- **Order of events:** PET came a median of
  `r num.fn(pathology$years_to_pet_median, 1)` years after the first smell
  test
- **Progression** is known only after the fact: the MCI groups describe
- **Small groups:** `r faster.dt$n` people with faster decline,
  `r pathology$tau_positive` tau positive, `r low$h3$main$events` with MCI
- **Several outcomes,** with no correction for multiple testing
- **MCI reviews** end in `r format(cog$mci$coverage_end, "%B %Y")`; later
  diagnoses are not counted
